Partial dependence of a prediction function on one input

Source: R/xpl.R
xppdp.Rd

The average prediction when one input is set to a value for every row and the others keep their values (Friedman 2001, sec. 8.2): at each value g of a grid, the mean of the predictions with column v set to g in every row. It is the effect of the input averaged over the data, as a risk tool's user would read it; where the input is correlated with the others it averages over combinations the data never hold, which xpale() avoids.

Usage

xppdp(x, f, v, y = NULL, grid = 20, gtype = c("even", "quant"), lctl = list())

# S3 method for class 'xppdp'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

The rows at which to predict: a numeric matrix, its column names those f sees, no missing values.

f

The prediction function: a function of a numeric matrix returning one finite number per row, or the names of learners of suplrn() ("glm", "lasso", "ridge", "enet", "forest").

v

The input: the name or the number of one column of x.

y

The outcome at the rows of x, needed only to fit the learners named in f.

grid

The number of grid points, one whole number from 2, or the values of the grid (at least two).

gtype

"even" for points evenly spaced over the column's range, "quant" for its quantiles.

lctl

The settings of the learners named in f: a list named by arguments of suplrn() (fam, nfold, fold, disc, alpha, nlam, nfin, ntree, mtry, seed); empty for a function.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class xppdp, a list: pd, a data frame with the grid (grid) and the partial dependence there (pd); term, the input's name; and n, the rows averaged.

Details

The grid is grid values of the column, evenly spaced from its minimum to its maximum (gtype = "even") or at its quantiles (gtype = "quant", quantile()'s default type 7, repeated values dropped), or the values given. The rows are written in the compiled core; f is called once on all of them.

References

Friedman, J. H. (2001). Greedy function approximation: a gradient boosting machine. Annals of Statistics, 29(5), 1189-1232. doi:10.1214/aos/1013203451

See also

xpcp() for the same curve for single rows, xpale().

Examples

set.seed(2)
x <- cbind(prior = rpois(100, 2), age = runif(100, 18, 60))
f <- function(m) plogis(-1 + 0.5 * m[, "prior"] - 0.03 * m[, "age"])
xppdp(x, f, "age", grid = 5)
#> xppdp: partial dependence on age, averaged over 100 rows
#>      grid        pd
#>  18.57225 0.3701719
#>  28.72549 0.3092730
#>  38.87872 0.2541271
#>  49.03196 0.2055543
#>  59.18520 0.1638529
